newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - European debt vols expected to nudge up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - European debt vols expected to nudge up.

text.p: Volatilities of options on European debt futures were steady on Monday but traders expected them to begin creeping higher as supply and U.S. data put the underlying markets on edge.
"For the European markets there is going to be a natural bid underneath the volatility," said a senior broker at GNI here.
Britain auctions 2.5 billion stg of 7.25 percent 2007 gilts on Tuesday, while Germany will top up its 6.0 percent 10-year bond with up 10 billion marks of supply, also on Tuesday.
U.S. data this week, including the fourth quarter employment cost index and GDP, will also put pressure on bonds, they said.

In Italy, talks resume between employers and unions in the engineering and metalworking industry to try to end a pay dispute. The industry accounts for 40 percent of Italy's industrial output and will set the tone for other pay deals.
"Bund vol has been fairly steady today," said the broker at GNI. "It's reached a level where it's hard for the volatility to go much lower."
He quoted volatility of Bund options were around 5.8/6.0 percent all the way out to June, little changed from Friday.
March Bund futures were quoted at 101.14 at 1217 GMT, unchanged from Friday's pit settlement.
"If the market breaks 101.00, (volatility) will show some pick up. You would expect the skew on out-of-the money puts to pick up," the broker said.
March gilt options were quoted at 7.9/8.0 percent, little changed from official LIFFE data from Friday.

"It's unlikely to slip much from those levels in the run up to next week's meeting," he said, referring to the February 5 monthly monetary meeting between Bank of England Governor Eddie George and Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.
A broker at a French investment house in London said trading in Bund options had been a mixed bag.
"It started off with a lot of call buying and call spread buying in March," he said.
He said one British investment house bought 1,000 lots of the 102.00/103.00 call spread, while a U.S. bank bought 2,000 lots of par puts.
"The main thing is paper buying options, there's no real direction to it," he said.
